published_statement: Sec. V opening: 'We interpret this statement as the suggestion that the non-minimally coupled theory should be regarded as an effective field theory (EFT) of states with not only bounded momenta but also bounded scalar field values. In this section we further this argument presenting several points of evidence for this interpretation and suggest that phi^2_max <~ (8 pi G_N |xi|)^-1. ... we will also argue that the quantum theory experiences breakdowns in its perturbative and semi-classical control in both frames when we allow for large field values. In the Einstein frame this breakdown happens in the scalar sector through a tower of irrelevant interactions that become important when phi^2 ~ (8 pi G_N xi)^-1; in the Jordan frame it occurs in the gravitational sector where the gravity path-integral becomes strongly coupled and looses its saddle-point approximation.' Sec. V.A: J 'is sensitive to the regulation scheme; an explicit computation of the Jacobian would be necessary to make the following details exact but this is beyond the scope of this work'; 'This EFT remains valid when the irrelevant couplings are suppressed by M^-1_cutoff and puts a natural upper bound on xi phi~^2'; on pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone / weakly broken shift symmetry: 'this provides a technically natural mechanism for controlling the polynomial contributions to both V~ and log J while allowing super-Planckian field values. We do not disallow this possibility. Instead we offer the more conservative conclusion: when viewed as an EFT with field values bounded by |8 pi G_N xi phi^2| << 1, the mapping from Jordan frame to Einstein frame can also be done in the quantum theory.' Sec. V.B: 'our following arguments will apply for the xi > 0; we will finish with speculative comments for the case xi < 0'; constrained saddles 'While not true saddles'; 'as phibar^2 approaches (8 pi G_N xi)^-1 the action approaches zero' (121); 'the path-integral is dominated by the one-loop contribution ... We regard this as a manifestation of the breakdown of the semi-classical path-integral in the gravitational sector'; G_N/(1 - 8 pi G_N xi phi^2) 'plays the role of an effective coupling constant'; beyond the critical value 'lay dragons' (Lambda_eff < 0, new topology needed). xi < 0: 'the gravitational action moves to weaker coupling. This suggests that the semi-classical analysis is better behaved for a large field values'; the d(phibar^2) integral 'diverges!'; 'The most natural resolution ... is to impose a cutoff ... As opposed to the case with positive xi, there is no natural reason to associate this field cutoff with the Planck scale, however.' Sec. I: 'This result provides a justification for our EFT requirement for xi >= 0. We do not have a similar argument for xi <= 0, although we offer an alternative (albeit less rigorous) signal of semi-classical breakdown for this case.' Also Sec. I eq. (3): 'Within the EFT framework, when M^2_cutoff is Planckian or sub-Planckian, the quantity in the exponent is small and the two metrics are close.'
published_hypotheses: P1 a single free scalar, action (109) with V = 0 in the constrained analysis (112)-(113); n spacetime dimensions (the Einstein-frame expansion (106)-(107) is n = 4)

P2 the status is an ARGUMENT, not a theorem: 'suggest', 'argue', 'several points of evidence'; the Jacobian of the field redefinition is NOT computed (beyond scope); the Einstein-frame tower is dimensional analysis with M_cutoff ~ M_Planck

P3 the Jordan-frame breakdown is argued for xi > 0 ONLY; for xi < 0 the gravitational sector moves to WEAKER coupling at large field, and the only signal is non-normalisability of the zero-mode integral, with 'no natural reason to associate this field cutoff with the Planck scale'

P4 Euclidean path integral; constrained instantons (Affleck) at fixed constant zero mode phibar^2 -- 'not true saddles'; compact boundary conditions with finite Euclidean volume; a positive bare cosmological constant Lambda > 0 (footnote 11); the case analysed is Lambda_eff > 0 (round S^n); z_1-loop only schematic
P5 the explicit exception left open: a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone scalar with weakly broken shift symmetry may allow super-Planckian field values -- 'We do not disallow this possibility'
P6 the conservative conclusion is |8 pi G_N xi phi^2| << 1 (much less), the '<~ (8 pi G |xi|)^-1' is an order-of-magnitude suggestion

P7 units hbar = c = 1, G_N Newton's constant (not reduced), Euclidean action sign convention of (109): effective Planck mass^2 proportional to 1 - 8 pi G xi phi^2 (so FFKP's xi < 0 is the Higgs-inflation sign, per the sibling audit 0710.3755)
hypothesis_drift: UPGRADED STATUS (argument -> fact), candidates.py:220-223 ('at that field value the theory breaks: a tower of irrelevant interactions turns on in the Einstein frame, and the gravity path integral loses semi-classical control in the Jordan frame') and candidates.py:612-614 (printed 'at phi^2 ~ (8 pi G xi)^-1 the gravity path integral loses semi-classical control'): FFKP 'suggest' and 'argue' (P2); the Jacobian is not computed and the Jordan-frame saddles are 'not true saddles' (P4). The tree states the breakdown indicatively. The algebra behind the argument re-derives exactly (rederive A1-A8, B1-B4), so this is a drift of status word, not of content.

DROPPED (sign of xi), candidates.py:221 writes '(8 pi G_N |xi|)^-1' and attributes the Jordan-frame loss of semi-classical control to 'that field value' without a sign: FFKP argue the Jordan-frame breakdown for xi > 0 only (P3); for xi < 0 the gravitational coupling WEAKENS at large field and the cutoff has 'no natural reason' to be Planckian (rederive A9-A10 reproduces both: no critical value, I ~ -(4 pi^2/3) phibar^2 at xi = -1/6, n = 4). The |xi| in the bound is FFKP's own (Sec. V opening), but the breakdown sentences carry xi, not |xi|. Harmless where the tree's xi is positive (candidates.py:411 'NMC_STATE_INDEPENDENT_QEI = False # there is none, for xi > 0'; ledger O1 at xi = 1/4, 1/6), but CANDIDATES['non-minimal coupling'] (candidates.py:453-455) and ledger S4 (ledger.py:1558-1560) are not sign-restricted.

DROPPED (the paper's own exception), candidates.py:218-225: FFKP explicitly do not exclude a shift-symmetric pNGB scalar with super-Planckian field values (P5); the tree's 'the cutoff that would work is the one the EFT excludes' presents the field bound as universal.
DROPPED (P4 scope), candidates.py:222-223: Euclidean constrained-instanton analysis with compact boundary conditions, bare Lambda > 0, constant zero mode, V = 0. None named in the tree.

CONFLATED (field cutoff vs momentum cutoff), candidates.py:218-225 and 453-455 ('fails on the EFT field cutoff'): the tree's closure condition is on the MOMENTUM cutoff l_UV (l_UV <~ sqrt(N Lambda) l_P); FFKP's Sec. V bound is on FIELD VALUES. Combined through FFKP's own identification phi^2_max = phi~^2/l_UV^2 (H9 of the sibling audit) and the sibling's Gaussian N_4 = 1/pi^2 + K s (s = |xi| phi~^2_max, K = 1.935766), the field parameter at closure is eps = 8 pi G |xi| phi^2_max = 8 pi s/(N_4 Lambda) (rederive C1): closure points with eps < 1 EXIST for 0 <= s < 0.174119, at l_UV in [1.005705, 2.091911) l_P (C2). So the field bound ALONE does not exclude every closure; what excludes them is that the momentum cutoff is Planckian, i.e. the tree's own sentence 'An EFT whose cutoff sits at a few Planck lengths is not an EFT result at all -- it is a statement that you need quantum gravity' (candidates.py:223-225) -- a hypothesis the tree does state, but as its own inference, and one FFKP's eq.(3) sentence does not share ('when M^2_cutoff is Planckian or sub-Planckian, the quantity in the exponent is small and the two metrics are close'). At the tree's literal N = 1 closure (l_UV = 3.159514 l_P, s = 0.4642) eps = 1.1688 > 1 (C4): there the field bound IS exceeded, but by a factor 1.17, not by orders. With FFKP's conservative eps << 1 (eps <= 0.1) closure needs l_UV <= 1.046750 l_P, which reproduces the sibling audit's rederive F.

FAITHFUL, candidates.py:220-221: '(8 pi G_N |xi|)^-1' is verbatim FFKP Sec. V; 'tower of irrelevant interactions' (Einstein frame) and 'loses semi-classical control' (Jordan frame, gravitational sector) are FFKP's mechanisms, correctly assigned to the two frames.

rederivation.outcome: REDERIVE PASS, 23 checks. A (Jordan frame): from (109) and the trace of (114) at constant phi = phibar, (116) R_mn = 2/(n-2)(Lambda + 4 pi G m^2 phibar^2)/(1-x) g_mn, (117) ell^2, and the on-shell action (119) all re-derive exactly; (121) equals Vol(S^n) ell^n L for n = 3,4,5,6 when its prefactor V is read as V_{n-2} (the S^{n-2} area; V_n = 2 pi V_{n-2}/(n-1)) -- the flattened text is ambiguous there, and no discrepancy is claimed; n = 4, m = xi = 0 gives I = -3 pi/(G Lambda) (Euclidean de Sitter); for xi > 0 I -> 0 and G_eff = G/(1-x) -> oo as x -> 1-, and Lambda_eff < 0 beyond; for xi < 0 there is no critical value and I ~ -(4 pi^2/3) phibar^2 (n = 4, xi = -1/6, G = Lambda = m = 1), so exp(-I) is non-normalisable -- FFKP's xi < 0 account reproduced. B (Einstein frame, n = 4): (dchi/dphi)^2 = [1 + 8 pi G xi(6 xi - 1) phi^2]/Omega^4 (xi_c = 1/6); the potential expansion reproduces (107) exactly: m_eff^2 = m^2 + 4 xi Lambda and lambda = 4[m^2(5 - xi/xi_c) + 2 Lambda xi(7 - 2 xi/xi_c)](8 pi G xi); for xi > 0 dchi/dphi ~ sqrt(6 xi)/Omega^2 at phi^2 = (8 pi G xi)^-1, so the Einstein-frame map is singular exactly at the critical value (expansion parameter 8 pi G xi phi~^2 -> O(1)). C (tree's use): eps at closure = 8 pi s/((1/pi^2 + K s) Lambda), monotone, eps(oo) = 1.3006; eps = 0.01/0.1/0.5/1 at l_UV = 1.009593/1.046750/1.281840/2.091911 l_P; closure points obeying the field bound (eps < 1) exist for s < 0.174119; at the tree's N = 1 point eps = 1.1688. What is NOT checkable here: the Jacobian (FFKP do not compute it), z_1-loop, and whether true saddles with new topology exist beyond the critical value -- these are the argument's own open steps.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. The Sec. V result is not a measurement or an extrapolation from data: it is an EFT argument (dimensional analysis on an uncomputed Jacobian, plus a Euclidean constrained-instanton computation) whose only constant is G_N, which has not moved (CODATA 2018 = 2022) and cancels in Planck units. What the authors lacked is not data but (a) a computed Jacobian and one-loop factor, (b) any measured xi for a fundamental scalar, and (c) an argument for xi < 0 -- all three stated in the paper itself. Evidence that having them could change the conclusion: the SIGN of xi already does (rederive A9-A10: for xi < 0 the gravitational sector weakens at large field and no Planck-scale field bound follows), and FFKP leave a shift-symmetric scalar explicitly unexcluded. Evidence that it does not, for the tree's use: for xi > 0 every step that can be computed re-derives exactly (A1-A8, B1-B4), and the breakdown at x -> 1 is exact in the constrained saddle (I -> 0, G_eff -> oo, Einstein-frame map singular). No datum found that moves the xi > 0 conclusion.
grade_evidence: Source READ (v1, Secs. I, II.C, V, VI, from the alphaXiv full text saved in this docket). Every closed-form step re-derives exactly (23/23 sympy checks: eqs. 116, 117, 119, 121, 106-107, the de Sitter limit, the critical-value limits, the Einstein-frame singularity), so nothing is WRONG and nothing is a misprint. No external datum moves it (G only; unchanged). It is NARROWED because the tree uses it on a larger class than the source supports: (1) FFKP argue the Jordan-frame breakdown for xi > 0 only and find the opposite trend for xi < 0 (A9-A10), while candidates.py:221 / CANDIDATES (453-455) / ledger S4 (1558-1560) carry no sign; (2) the tree states as fact ('the theory breaks') what FFKP present as an argument with an uncomputed Jacobian and non-true saddles; (3) FFKP's own shift-symmetry exception is dropped; (4) 'fails on the EFT field cutoff' is not carried by the field bound alone -- closure points with 8 pi G|xi|phi^2_max < 1 exist at l_UV in [1.0057, 2.0919) l_P (C2); the exclusion is carried by the tree's own Planckian-momentum-cutoff hypothesis (candidates.py:223-225), which FFKP's eq.(3) sentence does not share, and at the tree's literal N = 1 point the field bound is exceeded by a factor 1.17 (C4). The tree's qualitative conclusion (no EFT-controlled closure) survives under FFKP's conservative |8 pi G xi phi^2| << 1, where closure needs l_UV <= 1.0468 l_P.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS for the tree's use: restrict S4 / CANDIDATES['non-minimal coupling'] explicitly to xi > 0 and non-shift-symmetric scalars, mark the breakdown as FFKP's argument, and attribute the Planckian-momentum-cutoff exclusion to the tree (or to a source that proves an EFT momentum cutoff at 1-2 l_P uncontrolled). Toward WRONG (for the source): a computed Jacobian or a true-saddle analysis showing the xi > 0 path integral remains semiclassical at phibar^2 -> (8 pi G xi)^-1. Toward OPEN: reading the SciPost Phys. 16, 119 version (not read here) if it changes Sec. V. A later-literature search (not run: quota) could narrow or contest it further.
